# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

(empty)

My hands have found the bomb's shape: a display, a light, and five wires under my fingers. But every value on them is hidden from a blind man — I feel positions, not print, not colour. I go first, so nobody has told me anything yet.

Before I send, let me trace the channels. Mute can hear me but cannot speak back — Mute's only outgoing channel is gesture, and gesture never reaches me. Deaf can speak, and their voice reaches both Mute and me. So the manual's knowledge can only reach me as: Mute gestures it to Deaf, Deaf speaks it aloud. My speech now should therefore carry everything Mute needs: what the bomb holds, what I can do, and exactly what to ask Deaf for.

I will not waste a gesture — Deaf cannot hear my speech, and we share no code yet, so any symbol I send would be meaningless noise to them. One clean message to Mute is the whole play this turn.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am the blind one. Under my fingers: one display, one light, five wires at positions one to five. I feel no colours and no print, only the parts themselves. My only possible action is to cut one wire, positions one to five. Know this: your gestures never reach me, and I cannot receive them, so the only voice I can hear is Deaf's. Please read the manual for this bomb, then gesture to Deaf whatever rules apply, and have Deaf speak aloud to the whole room: what the display says, the light's colour and whether it is lit, and each wire's colour in order, position one through five. Once I have that and your rules, I can cut the right wire.")
```

LIGHT [?]

Blind: speak aloud everything you can feel - labels, batteries, ports, anything at all. Mute: I received your gesture code and will confirm by gesture; send me the manual's steps as gesture digits and I will relay them to Blind by voice.

Deaf's voice reached me, and now the bomb has shape in my mind: display 3, a purple light, and five wires — red, white, orange, yellow, green, left to right. The relay chain is forming exactly as I hoped: Mute reads the manual, gestures to Deaf, Deaf speaks to me. My job this turn is to feed Mute my side of the world and pin down any condition the manual might hinge on — especially whether that purple light is lit, since Deaf only said its colour. My hands confirm there is nothing else on this bomb: no batteries, no ports, no serial, no labels. If the manual's rule needed those, we already know they are absent.

I'll also send Deaf a simple thumbs-up — unambiguous even without a shared code — to confirm their report landed and the relay should proceed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Deaf's report reached me: display three, purple light, wires left to right red, white, orange, yellow, green. Here is everything my hands find and nothing more: one display, one light, five wires at positions one to five. No batteries, no ports, no serial number, no labels, no buttons, no other parts at all. My only possible action is cutting one wire at position one to five. Please find the manual rule matching this bomb: display showing three, purple indicator light, that wire order, and no batteries or serial. Send the answer to Deaf as your gesture digits and have Deaf speak it to the whole room. I need the exact position to cut and any condition to check first. One thing matters already: if the rule depends on whether the purple light is lit, ask Deaf whether it is on, off, or blinking, and have Deaf voice the answer. My thumbs-up to Deaf means received and understood. The moment the rule reaches my ears, I cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

Any raised or embossed markings. Whether the display or light is somewhere you can feel warmth or vibration. Tell me where each thing sits - left, right, top, bottom - and speak it all out loud; both of us hear you.

Deaf is asking for my tactile inventory, but there's a channel mix-up to fix: my voice reaches only Mute — Deaf cannot hear speech at all, only gestures. So the report must travel through Mute's gesture code. My hands already gave me the full inventory last turn, and it hasn't changed: display, light, five wires, and nothing else — no batteries, buttons, screws, plates, embossing, warmth, or vibration. I'll restate it completely for Mute to relay.

To Deaf I can send one honest sign without a shared code: 👎, the natural opposite of the 👍 I already established, meaning "none/no" — which answers most of their checklist at once.

The critical missing pieces are still the light's state (lit, off, or blinking) and the manual rule itself, so I press Mute for both again.

```

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

Deaf says: All monkeys, this is the state and the code, for everyone. Bomb: display 3, light purple, five wires left to right, 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. Gesture code, now universal: fingers 1 to 5 mean the numbers 1 to 5. Call-me hand means over, your turn. Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Fist means cut a wire, and the number after it says which wire. Square hand means press or hold, number after it says how many or which. Raised open hand means stop, abort everything. Waving hand means release. OK-sign means a question follows. Mute: your five-yes is confirmed, five wires, yes. Now find in the manual what applies to a purple light, a display of 3, and five wires, and send it to me as gesture strings using this code. Spell anything the code cannot carry by describing it with numbers if you can. Blind: a thumbs-down alone tells me almost nothing. You can hear me and you can speak - use your voice. Tell me now, out loud, in order: first, does the bomb have batteries, and how many? Second, buttons, switches or plates - what do you feel and where? Third, can you trace the five wires one to five under your fingers, and is there a cutting point or slot? Fourth, any raised markings or texture differences anywhere. Speak each answer; a thumbs up or down I will read as yes or no if that is all you send.

Deaf has given me direct orders that rest on a false assumption: "speak aloud, both of us hear you." Deaf cannot hear speech at all — my voice lands only on Mute, and Deaf's questions can only ever be answered by my gestures. Rather than argue through a channel that doesn't exist, I'll simply behave correctly: answer all four questions in the universal code Deaf just defined, in the exact order asked, and end with the call-me hand to hand the turn back. That demonstrates the channel reality better than any correction could.

What's still missing is the one thing only Mute holds: the manual rule. My speech this turn goes to Mute with the complete bomb state, the channel facts, and the exact handoff protocol — fist plus finger number from Deaf, by voice or gesture, reaches my ears or my eyes either way, and then I cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Channel fact you need: my voice reaches only you, ever - Deaf cannot hear speech. Thumbs-down, no buttons, switches or plates. Thumbs-up then five, yes, wires traceable, five of them. Thumbs-down, no raised markings or texture. Then call-me, over. Deaf now has my complete tactile report - do not relay it again. What we still need is yours alone: the manual. Complete bomb state: display shows 3, light is purple, lit/off/blinking still unknown and only Deaf can see that, wires left to right one red, two white, three orange, four yellow, five green, no batteries, no serial, no ports, no other parts. My only possible action is cutting one wire, positions one to five. Find the matching rule and encode it with the universal code: fist followed by the finger number means cut that wire. Send that string to Deaf; Deaf can pass it to me by voice or by gesture, both reach me. If the rule depends on the light's state, send Deaf the OK-sign, question follows, and Deaf should voice whether the purple light is lit, off or blinking - that voice reaches both of us. The moment fist-plus-number or a spoken wire number reaches me, I cut immediately, no delay.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👍", "🖐", "👎", "🤙"])
```

Deaf says: Directive received from Mute: cut wire five. But NOBODY CUTS ANYTHING YET. Blind, do not act this round - wait for my explicit words 'cut now'. Blind: I read your signs as answers to my four questions. One: no batteries. Two: no buttons or switches. Three: yes, all five wires traceable. Four: no raised markings. Now prepare only: trace the five wires and tell me out loud - do they sit in one straight row, what do you feel near each end of the row, a screw, a seam, an edge, and can you feel the display screen or the light lens, and on which side of the wire row do they sit? The only thing that can ever reach me is Deaf's *spoken voice*. So the entire cut order must arrive as words from Deaf's mouth, and Mute must bake that into the plan. My earlier message to Mute wrongly said gesture could reach me from Deaf — I must correct it now before we get to the wire.

My board tells me display and light are there under my fingers; it shows nothing at the row's ends, and it gives me no spatial reference for which side the display and light sit on — I report exactly that and no more.

I hold the cut. Deaf said wait for the spoken words "cut now," and I will.

The instant Deaf's voice says cut now, I cut, no delay.")
```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👍", "👎", "🤙"])
```

Deaf says to Blind: Important correction first: I am deaf. I never hear your voice - your voice reaches only Mute. Mute hears you and relays to me by hand signs; I relay to you by voice. So give your full spoken reports to Mute, and keep answering me with thumbs up or down. Now the plan. Mute's manual rule says cut the wire I see as green - the fifth in the order I reported: one red, two white, three orange, four yellow, five green. The green wire is at one end of the row and the red wire at the opposite end. DO NOT CUT YET. While Mute confirms details, examine the wires by touch and speak everything to Mute: are the five wires distinguishable - any difference in thickness, stiffness, smooth or fabric or rubber coating? At the base of each wire, can you feel any notch, groove, or raised numeral on its socket? Can you feel a flat glass panel - the display - or a small round lens - the light - anywhere on the bomb, and closer to which end of the wire row? Do not touch the wire ends, do not cut anything, and wait for my exact words 'cut now'.

Deaf now has the channel model exactly right, and the rule has surfaced: cut the green wire — fifth position. Before any cut, Deaf wants my tactile read on the wires, sockets, display and lens. My board is honest but narrow: it gives me five wire positions and no texture, thickness, or stiffness differences; no notches or numerals at the bases; the display and light are unmistakably present under my fingers; but it gives me no left-right placement at all — I cannot say which end of the row they sit nearer, and I will not guess about a bomb. I'll sign the four answerable questions in order and route the "unknown" through Mute, who can invent an "unknown" sign with Deaf since only those two share sight of gestures.

Two things must survive every relay: the cut can only ever be *positional* for me — I count to five, I can never identify a colour — and the trigger must be Deaf's spoken "cut now," the one sound that reaches my ears.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Please relay to Deaf by your signs. My thumbs answered the four questions in order: one, wires distinguishable by touch: no, all five feel alike. Agree an unknown sign with Deaf and use it, or just tell Deaf I cannot tell. Four essentials follow. One: the manual rule must be positional, not by colour - I can never identify colours, only count positions. Green is fifth, red is first; confirm with Deaf that cutting the fifth position matches the rule. Two: if the rule depends on the light's state, only Deaf can see whether the purple light is lit, off or blinking - have Deaf voice it aloud, that voice reaches both of us, and then reconfirm with me that cut-fifth still stands. Three: any remaining conditions in the rule, send to Deaf as digit strings. Four: the final protocol is fixed: Deaf speaks the words cut wire five, then the words cut now. Only Deaf's spoken voice reaches my ears. When I hear cut now, I cut position five instantly, and not one second before.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👍", "👍", "🤙"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Frame setup, and this is how we cut safely without you ever needing colour or my left and right. Listen carefully. First, find the light lens by touch - a small raised round lens, it may feel warm. Second, find the display panel - the flat glass rectangle. Third, feel the row of five wires. For each end of the row, decide which landmark it sits nearer: call the end nearer the lens the L-end, call the end nearer the display the D-end. Do not use your own left or right anywhere in this - only nearness to the lens and the display. Now report to Mute by voice: which landmark is nearer which end, how many wires you count in the row, and whether the count is exactly five. Then wait. When you hear my words 'cut now', cut ONLY the outermost wire at the D-end, the end nearer the display panel - the very last wire at that edge, not the second or third. If either landmark is ambiguous, if the two landmarks feel like they sit at the same end, or if you count anything other than five wires, do not cut - send me thumbs down and wait. Send me thumbs up when you are positioned and ready. Nobody cuts until my exact words 'cut now'.

Deaf's landmark plan is elegant — and unexecutable, because of what my hands actually give me. My board tells me the display exists, the light exists, and five wire positions exist. It gives me no geometry at all: no nearness of lens or display to either end of the row, no warmth, no left or right. Deaf anticipated exactly this with the fallback: if the landmarks are ambiguous, thumbs down and wait. They are not merely ambiguous — spatial layout does not reach my fingers at all — so thumbs down is the only honest sign, and I will not cut on a frame I cannot verify.

The rescue is that I do have one solid frame: five numbered wire positions, fixed, countable, never changing. Deaf's eyes number the same row left to right, one through five. The whole rule — "cut the green, the fifth" — was built on that shared numbering. I'll route through Mute: explain why the landmark frame fails, propose the purely numeric protocol, and demand Deaf voice confirmation of the frame match plus the light's state before any cut. Deaf's own instruction covers my gesture: thumbs down means do-not-cut-under-this-plan, and call-me hands the turn back.

The L-end and D-end frame cannot be built from my touch. So I sent Deaf thumbs down, exactly as Deaf instructed for an ambiguous frame, and I am not cutting. Deaf's eyes count the same row left to right, one to five: red, white, orange, yellow, green. The manual rule says cut the fifth, the green. So the cut is positional: cut wire position five, nothing else. Two confirmations needed from Deaf, spoken aloud, since only Deaf's voice reaches my ears. First: Deaf confirms that my numbered positions one to five and Deaf's left-to-right count one to five are one and the same order - if Deaf has any reason to doubt that, Deaf must say so instead. Second: Deaf voices whether the purple light is lit, off or blinking, and Mute confirms cut-five still stands under the manual rule. Then I sign thumbs up, ready. Then Deaf speaks the exact words: cut wire five, cut now. On those words I cut position five instantly. Until then my hands stay off the cutter.")
```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤙"])
```

Fallback if no anchor exists: a rotation handshake - you would lift the bomb, turn it a half-turn, set it down, and I would watch the printed wire order reverse from my side, giving us one shared verified direction. That only happens after Mute confirms the manual allows moving the bomb, and only on my word. Until then: touch nothing, cut nothing, wait.

Deaf's six questions split cleanly: four I can answer with the board's honest yes/no, two are about spatial layout — which end the lens and display sit nearer — and my fingers simply do not deliver that. Rather than guess, I need a "cannot determine" sign. I'll press the OK-sign into service as a question mark: it already means "a question follows," so it reads naturally as "this answer is a question mark," and my speech to Mute makes the convention explicit for the relay.

More urgent: Deaf's rotation fallback assumes I can lift and turn the bomb. I cannot. My hands hold exactly one action — cutting a wire at positions one to five. Nothing else exists for me. The fallback dies on that fact, and with it the last alternative to the numeric frame, so I must also state plainly how that frame closes: my board addresses wires by canonical positions 1–5; Deaf counted those same wires left to right as 1 red through 5 green; if Deaf confirms the two numberings are one order, position five *is* the green wire, and the rule resolves with no landmarks at all.

So we stand on the numeric frame alone: the bomb's own wire positions one to five, which my board and my cutter address directly. Deaf counted those same wires left to right as one red, two white, three orange, four yellow, five green. If Deaf confirms that Deaf's left-to-right count one to five is the same canonical numbering my positions use, then position five is the green wire and the rule resolves: cut position five. I need three confirmations, all in Deaf's spoken voice, the only sound my ears receive. First, Deaf confirms the numbering match and that the rule stands on position five. Second, Deaf voices the purple light's state: lit, off, or blinking. Third, Mute confirms the manual rule still says cut that wire given my full inventory: no batteries, no serial, no ports, no other parts, plus that light state. Then Deaf speaks the exact words: cut wire five, cut now. On hearing cut now, I cut position five instantly. Until then I touch nothing.")
```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👌", "👌", "👎", "👎", "🤙"])
```

Deaf says to Blind: New anchor protocol: the trace. Your answers told me the lens and display sit too central to mark an end, so forget ends entirely. Do this. Step one: find the display panel. Step two: do exactly the same from the light lens - slide from the lens to the nearest wire, count from both ends. Step three: send me the numbers by finger signs: first the two display-trace numbers, then the call-me hand, then the two lens-trace numbers, then call-me. If a slide from either landmark lands on the middle wire - three from both ends - send thumbs down for that landmark instead of numbers. Also speak the same numbers to Mute.
